title: Reconcile out-of-order payloads in metering pipeline with heuristic reconciliation
creator: Leah Chen
description: Intermittent customer reports and internal audits show token accounting divergence when websocket- and multipart-based streaming requests deliver fragments out of chronological order. The metering pipeline assumes near-monotonic fragment offsets for attribution; when fragments are delayed, retried, or multiplexed by proxies, we either double-credit, miss-credit, or attribute tokens to the wrong session. This ticket investigates a pragmatic, low-risk heuristic reconciliation layer that operates in the ledger finalizer to correct common out-of-order cases without requiring a full protocol redesign. Goals: (1) define a canonical reconciliation window and matching heuristics for fragment reorder, (2) implement a best-effort idempotency / dedupe pass for late fragments, (3) add telemetry and reconciliation metrics to validate behavior, and (4) create a safe rollout that can be toggled per-tenant.
comments: 2026-01-15 - Leah Chen: Triage: repro'd with internal replay harness. Repro steps attached in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ORD-580901. Initial theory: proxy reordering + client retries cause non-monotonic fragment offsets.

2026-01-18 - Rajat Kulkarni: Investigation: added local simulation harness that injects fragments with delays and out-of-order offsets. Observed three failure modes: duplicate credits, orphaned finalization (missing final chunk), and attribution to previous session id when session IDs recycled quickly.

2026-01-22 - Rajat Kulkarni: Design options evaluated: Option A: strict sequence numbers enforced at ingress (requires client changes) — high bar. Option B: ledger-side reconciliation window that re-evaluates last N minutes of fragments for sessions that finalized within window — lower risk. Option C: maintain full per-session fragment reassembly state until long tail expires — costly memory impact. Recommend B with conservative defaults and adaptive heuristics.

2026-01-27 - Product (Maya Rao): PM review: prioritize low blast radius. Recommend per-tenant feature flag and instrumentation before general rollout. Add acceptance criteria around no increase in false-negatives for billed tokens.

2026-01-30 - Eng (Rajat): Implementation: added reconciler prototype that scans the finalization window (default 90s) and applies idempotent dedupe rules: (1) fuzzy match on encoded-length+hash for payloads, (2) accept late fragment if it fills a gap and total credits move closer to canonical tokenizer result, (3) reject if it retroactively increases billed tokens beyond threshold delta (safety guard). Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3214 (proto branch).

2026-02-03 - Eng (QA): Integration test added to harness. Created synthetic scenarios: multiplexed clients, proxy reorder, partial retransmit, compressed attachments. Early results: reconciler reduces double-credit rate by ~82% in synthetic workloads.

2026-02-06 - Design (Noah Kim): UX note for Console: reconciliation events should surface as 'finalization adjustments' in per-session logs and not appear as separate charges unless user inspects audit trail. Filed design ticket DES-9012 for Console change.

2026-02-09 - Eng (Rajat): Code review feedback received. Reviewer asks for stronger telemetry around false-positive rejections and a mechanism to opt out for compliance-sensitive tenants. Added metrics and feature flag CLI. Also noted blocker: staging needs a new client replayer to reproduce a particular late-chunk encoding seen in customer incident #INC-2026-17.

2026-02-09 - Leah Chen: Next steps: finish PR addressing review, add dashboard queries, schedule canary for a small set of internal accounts, and coordinate with Support for customer-facing messaging if we roll this broadly.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciler reduces duplicate-credit incidents in synthetic workload by >=75% compared to baseline
No increase in total billed tokens for 'steady-state' sessions beyond 0.5% (measured over 24h sample)
Feature flag exists to disable reconciler per-tenant and per-cluster
Reconciliation events are recorded in audit logs with original fragment ids and resulting delta
Unit/integration tests cover the three core failure modes: duplicate-credit, orphaned-finalization, wrong-session-attribution
test_plan: Unit tests: dedupe matcher (length/hash), gap-filler acceptance criteria, safety delta enforcement
Integration harness: replay recorded production fragments with injected reorders and compare ledgers with/without reconciler
Load test: run reconciler in a scaled staging environment under mixed small/large sessions to validate latency and memory overhead
Canary: enable for 2 internal tenants for 48h, evaluate metrics and support feedback
Post-rollout audit: run full daily audit query for 7 days to verify no regression in billed totals
telemetry_queries: SQL: SELECT count(*) AS dup_events, sum(delta_tokens) AS token_delta FROM metering.reconciliation WHERE created_at >= now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY dup_events DESC LIMIT 50;

SQL: SELECT session_id, final_billed_tokens, tokenizer_count FROM metering.finalized_sessions WHERE reconciled = true AND created_at >= now() - interval '1 day' ORDER BY ABS(final_billed_tokens - tokenizer_count) DESC LIMIT 200;
Grafana panel: reconciliation_success_rate = reconciler.accepted / reconciler.attempted (show per-tenant and 95th percentile)
Alert: reconciliation_false_positive_rate > 0.5% over 1h -> page on-call metering-eng
rollout_plan: Deploy reconciler to canary cluster behind feature flag (runtime flag 'reconciler.v1.enabled')
Enable for 'internal' and two low-volume tenants for 48 hours, monitor metrics and logs
If canary stable: expand to 10% of tenants with highest duplicate-credit incidence using rollout policy in Console
After 7 days of stable telemetery, flip global default to enabled and keep per-tenant opt-out for 30 days
If unexpected billing deltas occur, automatically rollback and create incident with audit data
blockers: Staging replay harness currently lacks a captured example of the exact compressed-attachment encoding observed in INC-2026-17. Need Support to provide raw capture or customer permission.
Console change DES-9012 required so that reconciliation events are visible; without it, customers will ask for contextual logs (blocked on small design/QA effort).
Performance review: memory overhead of scanning finalization window at scale needs formal benchmarking (ENG-Perf to run load test).
